recommendation.recommendation: Implement immediate flood irrigation to alleviate severe water stress and conduct rapid crop health inspection.
recommendation.justification: Satellite NDWI (-0.35) and ground data show no recent rainfall, creating critical water stress during the flowering stage. Immediate irrigation is required to restore soil moisture and protect yield, while a quick disease and nutrient check prevents secondary losses.
actions: Start flood irrigation today, applying ~30 mm of water per day for the next 3 days to raise soil moisture to at least 80 % of field capacity.
After the initial application, monitor soil moisture daily with tensiometers or moisture sensors and continue irrigation every 7‑10 days as needed to maintain optimal moisture.
Apply a balanced NPK fertilizer (e.g., 60‑30‑30) at the recommended rate to sustain nitrogen levels during vegetative growth.

Conduct a thorough visual inspection of the cotton canopy for Fusarium wilt, Verticillium wilt, aphid colonies, and bollworm damage; apply appropriate fungicides or insecticides if symptoms are observed.
Lay a thin layer of organic mulch (5‑10 cm) around the base of plants to reduce evaporation and protect exposed soil patches identified by high SAVI.
recommendation.expected_outcome: Restored soil moisture will eliminate critical water stress, preserving flower development and stabilising yield potential; early disease/nutrient scouting will prevent secondary yield losses, leading to a harvest comparable to the excellent NDVI baseline.
monitoring_plan: Record daily soil moisture readings and adjust irrigation schedule accordingly.
Weekly NDVI/NDWI checks via satellite or drone to verify canopy health and water status.
Bi‑weekly scouting for disease and pest symptoms; log any interventions applied.
Track irrigation volumes and fertilizer applications in a field log.
At the end of the flowering stage, compare actual yield estimates with baseline projections.
